```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 19
    n_vehicles = 4
    Q = 117  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[60, 63], [91, 81], [16, 43], [42, 63], [92, 21], [20, 48], [22, 83], [87, 75], [67, 20], [94, 65], [56, 58], [69, 57], [71, 5], [7, 19], [87, 82], [8, 77], [19, 65], [60, 58], [30, 93]]
    demands = [25, 13, 19, 12, 15, 19, 17, 10, 5, 17, 21, 16, 19, 21, 12, 23, 18, 10, 22]
    time_windows = [[0, 330], [35, 126], [58, 113], [48, 146], [27, 117], [53, 129], [49, 147], [67, 117], [51, 118], [36, 122], [68, 162], [34, 98], [28, 101], [54, 107], [51, 150], [58, 147], [52, 118], [53, 128], [32, 103], [46, 138]]
    service_times = [9, 5, 11, 6, 14, 10, 15, 12, 9, 6, 14, 5, 8, 7, 15, 15, 10, 12, 7]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

To: Dispatch, Fleet Operations, and Planning
From: Logistics Operations Manager
Subject: Routing and Scheduling Plan for Today’s Delivery Wave

Overview
We are planning a single-day delivery wave originating from our central depot using a fleet of identical vehicles. The task is to design efficient delivery routes that cover all scheduled customers across the service area while respecting delivery windows, vehicle capacity limits, and depot operating constraints.

Routing and Scheduling Challenge
- All deployed vehicles will begin their routes at the start of the shift (time 0), depart from the depot, visit a sequence of assigned customers, and then return to the depot before the end of the planning horizon (the depot’s latest acceptable return time).
- Each vehicle makes one continuous trip only; there are no mid-shift returns or secondary runs.
- Every customer must be visited exactly once. No split deliveries are allowed.
- Travel time between any two locations is the straight-line distance between their coordinates, with an implicit speed of 1 so that one unit of distance equals one unit of time.

Service and Timing Requirements
- Each customer has a delivery time window with an earliest and latest acceptable start-of-service time. Service must start within this window.
- If a vehicle arrives earlier than the window opens, it must wait until the window opens before beginning service.
- Each customer requires a specific unloading/service duration. The vehicle may depart a customer only after completing this service time. In other words, departure from a stop occurs at arrival time plus service time (or window open time plus service time if the vehicle arrived early and waited).
- All vehicles must complete their last customer and travel back to the depot in time to arrive before the depot’s closing time.

Capacity and Cost Considerations
- Vehicles are identical and have the same carrying capacity. The total customer demand assigned to any route must not exceed the vehicle’s capacity at any point.
- Using a vehicle incurs a fixed deployment cost, in addition to the distance-based travel cost. It may be more cost-effective to consolidate stops onto fewer routes if time windows and capacity allow, but not at the expense of on-time delivery or depot return requirements.

Goal
Develop a set of routes—one per deployed vehicle—that:
- Visit each customer exactly once.
- Respect all customer time windows, including waiting if a vehicle arrives early.
- Satisfy service time requirements at each stop.
- Keep the load on each vehicle within capacity throughout its route.
- Ensure every vehicle returns to the depot before the depot’s latest return time.
- Minimize total travel distance plus the fixed costs of the vehicles we deploy.

Deliverables
- A route plan for each deployed vehicle, listing stop sequence, planned arrival times, start-of-service times, and departure times.
- A summary of total distance traveled, number of vehicles used, and total estimated cost.
